title: To Retry or Not to Retry? That Is the Question.
why_read: A focused and well-reasoned benchmark idea testing whether AI models correctly judge if an HTTP request is safe to retry, a real and tricky distributed systems problem.
analysis: The author builds a benchmark around a narrow but practically important question: whether language models can correctly reason about retry safety for failed HTTP requests given status codes, idempotency keys, and timing. This is a genuinely subtle distributed systems problem, since naive retries can cause duplicate processing of POST requests or mask real failures. Framing an LLM evaluation around this kind of nuanced, real-world engineering judgment call is more interesting than generic coding benchmarks. The piece seems to combine solid systems knowledge with a reasonable evaluation methodology.
